units.text: Apple keeps improving its profiles feature on Apple TV 4K, and a change in tvOS 27 related to app access offers another reason to use profiles.
tvOS 27 lets you restrict users from launching specific apps
User profiles are a common feature of every major streaming service. They ensure viewers in a shared household can keep their viewing history and recommendations separate, among other benefits.
Apple has long had a profiles feature in tvOS, but it’s gotten a lot more useful in the past year thanks to several recent upgrades.
Now tvOS 27 has introduced another improvement. Per Apple’s official release notes:
Individual app controls in Settings let you block users from launching specific apps.
This change is clearly intended for parents.

Profiles for children can already limit the types of content they’ll see in the Apple TV app. That’s a useful feature, but it won’t keep your child from opening a different app with no such restrictions.
Now though, parents can open Settings and block certain apps from being launched at all when a child’s profile is active.
It’s a good step toward making profiles as full-featured as they deserve to be, and aligns with Apple’s recent focus in iOS 27 on upgrading parental controls.
On the subject of profile improvements, iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2 will bring Apple’s profile system to iPhone and iPad for the first time. You can read about that change here.
Do you use profiles on your Apple TV? What new features do you hope get added? Let us know in the comments.

units.text: The forthcoming iPhone Duo has more features than Apple has revealed, including a whole series of faces for its StandBy mode. Here's what to eventually look for.
While pre-orders for iPhone Duo don't start until October 16, and the Xcode betas still don't show developers everything, one has found many new options coming to iOS 27 for this device.

Developer pdfu reports that the Xcode 27.1 simulator is lacking Rushmore, an app that is for displaying the new StandBy faces. But despite that, they have managed to get certain of the new faces running.

Here's a deep dive into StandBy mode on iPhone Duo. Rushmore, the app meant to host the redesigned faces, is missing from the iOS 27.1 simulator. But its localization strings reveal unreported faces, and I got some new faces running in the current renderer. pic.twitter.com/lDQHOy5R0e
— pdfu (@itspdfu) September 28, 2026
These working ones are variants on familiar clock and calendar faces as used on the iPhone's current StandBy mode. But code references describe several more options.

Here's a deep dive into StandBy mode on iPhone Duo. Rushmore, the app meant to host the redesigned faces, is missing from the iOS 27.1 simulator. But its localization strings reveal unreported faces, and I got some new faces running in the current renderer. pic.twitter.com/lDQHOy5R0e
— pdfu (@itspdfu) September 28, 2026
Just because something is referenced in code, it doesn't necessarily mean that it will launch immediately. But those code references show five more faces:
Home Camera: up to nine camera views
Home Module
Flow
Fade
Snoopy
There are no details for Home Modular, Flow, or Fade. But the code for Flow also includes the term ResponsiveArt, which suggests that it will at least be an animated face.
Face editor
The iPhone Duo will also feature a revised editor for customizing these StandBy faces. It's very similar to the existing one on iPhone and is perhaps more like the Apple Watch face editor.
Users can swipe left and right to adjust, for instance, the style of an analog clock, its numerals, light mode and dark mode, plus the color of the face and the hands.
Some of these clock faces also have room for two widgets. Then some more are digital instead of analog and there pdfu has found code references for five layouts:
StandBy
Stacked
Top
Middle
Bottom
The presumption is that all but the StandBy one may actually be intended for when the iPhone is opened like a book.

Developer pdfu has a strong track record for examining beta code. They confirmed that the iPhone Duo would use Touch ID, for instance, and most recently uncovered that Siri could be replaced by Claude or ChatGPT.

units.text: Following two release candidates, Apple today released macOS Tahoe 26.7.1 and macOS Sequoia 15.8.1, as well as macOS 27.0.1. Here are the details.
macOS 27.0.1, macOS 26.7.1 and macOS 15.8.1 now available

After two release candidates, Apple is now rolling out macOS Tahoe 26.7.1 and macOS Sequoia 15.8.1, in addition to macOS 27.0.1 Golden Gate, the first update since the release of macOS 27 earlier this month.
Today’s releases come exactly one week after Apple rolled out the second round of release candidates, which also included public releases the following day.

Apple’s release notes during the RC mentioned only standard security fixes and performance improvements, but recent point releases have included significant security patches, many of which address vulnerabilities discovered with the help of AI tools.

Apple has even confirmed that the growing capabilities of AI tools are affecting its security release cadence. In June, the company said it had pushed out fixes originally planned for version 26.6 ahead of schedule because AI can speed up the development of malicious hacking tools, reducing the amount of time Apple wants to leave between making fixes public and getting them into users’ hands.
Apple will likely release the security details for macOS 27.0.1 Golden Gate, macOS Tahoe 26.7.1, and macOS Sequoia 15.8.1 in the coming hours, and we’ll report back with the noteworthy tidbits.
Update, 1:59 p.m. ET: Apple says macOS 27.0.1 Golden Gate “has no published CVE entries,” but says macOS Tahoe 26.7.1 and macOS Sequoia 15.8.1 fix the following issue:
CoreGraphics
Available for: macOS Sequoia

Impact: Processing a maliciously crafted file may lead to arbitrary code execution. Apple is aware of a report that this issue may have been exploited in an extremely sophisticated attack against specific targeted individuals on versions of iOS before iOS 27.
Description: An out-of-bounds write issue was addressed with improved bounds checking.
CVE-2026-86950: Meta Product Security
The release build for today’s macOS releases are:
macOS Sequoia 15.8: 24H32
macOS Tahoe 26.7.1: 25G241
macOS 27.0.1 Golden Gate: 26A5434
Did you spot anything new in today’s releases? Let us know in the comments.

evidence.title: First granular 27.0.1 updates arrive for IOS, macOS

units.text: The first granular updates to Apple's milestone operating system releases have arrived, with 27.0.1 updates now here for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, and visionOS.

Apple released its major yearly operating system revision on September 14, bringing iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, tvOS, and visionOS to the 27 generation. Two weeks later, Apple's released the first small update to the public.
The granular update is a minor version change, and is quite typical for Apple to release shortly after the main releases.
The new updates are:
iOS 27.0.1, build 24A446
iPadOS 27.0.1, build 24A446
macOS 27.0.1, build 26A434
watchOS 27.0.1, build 24R365
visionOS 27.0.1, build 24M372.
Apple also released granular updates to its earlier operating systems, too.
iOS 26.7.1, build 23H30
iPadOS 26.7.1, build 23H30
macOS 26.7.1, build 25G241
macOS 15.8.1, build 24H32.

At this early stage, it is unclear exactly what has changed with each operating system. However, while a granular release doesn't tend to have major feature changes, they usually include bug fixes and performance improvements for issues that emerge after launch.
This will probably include fixes for things like Neural Engine timeouts and Face ID kernel panics. For the latter, Apple confirmed a software update will fix the issue.

units.text: 9to5Mac is brought to you by CleanMyMac by MacPaw. With the release of macOS 27 Golden Gate, use CleanMyMac first to free up space, optimize your system, and ensure your new Mac runs at 100% on day one. Learn more.

One of the many new features included in macOS 27 Golden Gate is Safari’s new “Notify Me” feature, which lets users get alerted when a website updates content they’re interested in. Here’s how to use it.
Safari can now notify you when webpages change
One of the most useful ways Apple has incorporated Apple Intelligence into macOS 27 Golden Gate is through Safari’s new “Notify Me” feature.
With it, users can ask Safari to monitor a webpage for specific changes and receive a notification when it detects an update.
When setting up a new custom notification, in addition to telling Safari what to look for, the user can also set a regular schedule ranging from hourly to monthly.

After the custom notification is set up, Safari will check the webpage according to the selected schedule and notify the user when it detects the requested change, such as a price drop, an item coming back in stock, changes to policies, registrations opening, or new information being added to the page.
Setting up Safari’s new “Notify Me” feature:
On Safari, go to the webpage you want to keep an eye on.
Click the Page menu button to the right of the Smart Search field.
Select “Notify Me” from the pop-up menu.
In the “What should Safari look for?” field, describe what you want. Apple Intelligence will then analyze the page’s contents to determine whether it can handle your request.
Optionally, you can set how often and when Safari should check for updates. Hourly and Daily let you choose a specific time, while Weekly and Monthly also let you choose specific days.

Click Done. Alternatively, Safari may show a Next button instead. In that case, macOS will ask for permission to send Safari notifications. You can also manage Safari notification permissions from Settings > Notifications > Safari.
Importantly, since the feature relies on Apple Intelligence, it may not be available in all languages or regions. To check the current availability status, follow this link.

We've seen previews of iOS 27 running on the iPhone Duo, including a new StandBy mode that activates even when the iPhone isn't charging. Apple showed the mode in press materials, but leaker pdfu today shared a more in-depth look at some of the options.
There are multiple StandBy faces available on the ‌iPhone Duo‌, five of which we weren't aware of.
A Home Camera view will show a single camera feed or a grid of up to nine camera feeds. There's a Home Modular option that likely shows smart home controls, and a Snoopy-themed face.

A face editor will let users adjust the StandBy mode interface, choosing different styles and colors, similar to the existing iPhone StandBy customization screens. Swipe gestures are available for quick visual adjustments.
There are five widget layouts to choose from for clock faces that support widgets. The layouts include StandBy, Stacked, Top, Middle, and Bottom.
The ‌iPhone Duo‌ will be available for pre-order on October 16 ahead of an October 23 launch, and we'll likely see more details come out as we approach the release date.

N224 项目由苹果秘密项目部门（Special Projects Group）主导，该部门负责从概念到原型的早期开发。在 M2 机型发布至 M5 机型上市的 28 个月间，苹果继续坚持原有技术路线，并未加速推进其他设计。
目前爆料验证的 4 款原型机中，其中一款原型采用类似 Meta 的外部计算模块设计，将主要处理器置于头显之外的独立设备。这种设计可以减轻头显重量，同时维持高分辨率与广视野表现。
IT之家援引博文介绍，在研发 Vision Pro 头显过程中，苹果秉承“1,000 个‘不’换来一个‘是’”设计理念，期间经历打磨了多个原型产品，其中最值得关注的是 N107、N100 与 N109 三款原型：
N107 将计算任务卸载至外部设备如 Mac，视觉保真度较低，类似 XReal 眼镜。
N100 尝试将计算模块移至电池组，维持封闭式 VR 设计，代号“Vision Air”。
N109 则为更轻便、低成本版本，但搭载性能较弱的芯片。

evidence.title: New Vision Pro Headset: Apple Considering Four Different Concepts

units.text: New Vision Pro Headset: Apple Considering Four Different Concepts
Apple is working on a "completely revamped" Vision Pro headset that could go in any of four directions and likely won't arrive before late 2028 or early 2029, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman.

Writing in his latest Power On newsletter, Gurman said Apple's Vision team is exploring four concepts for the device, codenamed N224, including designs that offload internal components in a similar way to Meta's latest VR Glasses, which are expected to launch next spring.

An external computing module on Meta's device houses the battery and main processor, and can be clipped to the user's waist. Gurman, who has previewed Meta's headset, says the module is about the same size and weight as the current Vision Pro's battery pack, but with a grippy exterior.

Gurman reports that regardless of the Vision team's work, senior Apple decision-makers still consider the external puck concept as a "poor user experience" and want the company to stick with "something closer to an all-in-one design."

If any of this sounds familiar, that's because Gurman reported in June that Apple was still working on a cheaper, lighter successor to its Vision Pro headset. (The device-in-development is distinct from the long-rumored "Vision Air," which was cancelled last year.)

Apple knows it needs to come up with ways to simplify the design and make something cheaper and lighter, and it is said to be actively exploring ways to reduce the headset's weight by experimenting with plastic, titanium, other metals and various materials.

Still, Gurman has been told the work is on "life support" as the company focuses more on smart glasses, which it aims to release in late 2027. Despite the Vision Pro's most senior leaders "pressing their bosses to keep the category alive, funded and growing at Apple," Gurman says there's still no guarantee a new headset will ever launch.

evidence.title: The iPhone 18 Pro: The best and final iteration of the current form factor?

units.text: There’s a running joke that Apple always breathlessly announces that each year’s iPhone Pro is “the best iPhone we’ve ever made,” as if that were in some way surprising. But I do think that there’s some poignancy to the iPhone 18 Pro, because if the rumors about next year’s model are true, this could be the final iteration of the form factor that began with the iPhone X back in 2017.
Specifically, we’re expecting next year to see the next big step toward that “single slab of glass” vision which will end the era of evolutionary change we’ve seen over the last decade …
The evolution of the iPhone Pro models

If you were to line up every model from the iPhone 12 Pro to the iPhone 16 Pro, I think many people would struggle to tell the difference visually bar the switch from notch to Dynamic Island in 2022. The iPhone 17 Pro is still only an exception due to the extended camera island and Cosmic Orange option.

Of course, each model had new features, but I think even here it’s fair to say that unless a specific one has particular relevance to you personally, you really need to jump at least two or three generations before an upgrade amounts to a significantly better experience.

This in no way a criticism of Apple. The reality is that premium smartphones are a mature technology, at least in the conventional form-factor. We don’t see massive differences between successive generations because there’s only so much that can be done to improve them on an annual basis.

Apple is now experimenting with different form factors, starting with the iPhone Air and now, of course, the iPhone Duo – and we’re expecting another major design leap next year, in the form of a 20th anniversary model.

How exactly Apple will position next year’s design remains somewhat unclear. It was initially suggested that it would be a standalone model, distinct from the iPhone 19 Pro, while other reports suggest that it will be next year’s Pro model. There’s also the question of whether Apple will use sequential numbering or skip a number to mark the occasion, so it might instead be called the iPhone 20 Pro.

units.text: iPhone Duo will be here soon, so if you want to get a head start on accessories for Apple’s new model, here are our top recommendations.
Apple Pencil for handwritten notes, sketches, more
iPhone Duo is the first iPhone that will offer support for Apple Pencil, letting you jot handwritten notes, doodles, and more.
Apple Pencil will be supported on iPhone Duo later this year via a software update. But when support comes, Apple says it will require an Apple Pencil (USB-C). No other Pencil models are compatible.
iPhone Duo will let you use Apple Pencil both on its outer and inner displays. The design of Apple’s first foldable was even inspired by the proportions of a standard A-series paper notebook.
Apple Pencil (USB-C): now only $69 (down from $79)
Power adapter for fast charging iPhone Duo
iPhone Duo supports fast charging, letting you charge up to 50 percent in just 20 minutes.
But in order to get the fastest charging speeds, you’ll need the right power adapter.
Apple’s 40W Dynamic Power Adapter with 60W Max supports iPhone Duo fast charging, and a great third-party alternative is Anker’s 100W power brick.

Like other models, iPhone Duo doesn’t come with a power adapter in the box—only a USB-C cable. Most of us have 20W chargers lying around, but if you want to get a power adapter that supports the quickest iPhone Duo charging, these two products are my recommendations.
Apple 40W Dynamic Power Adapter with 60W Max: only $34 (down from $39)
Anker 100W USB-C Charger with 5FT Cable: $29
MagSafe Car Mount for when you’re on the go
One of my top iPhone accessory recommendations is ESR’s MagSafe Car Mount. I’ve used it for years, and it should prove a great accessory for iPhone Duo too.

With a MagSafe car mount, your iPhone has a secure place to stay while on the go. MagSafe provides a strong magnetic attachment, and you can clip the mount to your A/C vent so it’s made visible and easy to reach as needed.

I like combining my iPhone with CarPlay when driving, so that in Apple Maps I can get the navigation map on my in-vehicle CarPlay screen while the iPhone shows my full step-by-step directions. I expect this to be even better with the iPhone Duo’s large screen.
ESR MagSafe Car Mount: only $19 (down from $29)
iPhone Duo cases
Apple isn’t yet selling its new $129 iPhone Duo Folio with Kickstand. But if you’re looking to buy a far more affordable iPhone Duo case, there are plenty of third-party options already available.
Buying an iPhone Duo case not only gets you ready for October 23, it’s also a nice way to preview the size and shape of the iPhone Duo before committing $1,999 or more.
I haven’t tested these cases, but here are some options I’m interested in.
SPIDERCASE Magnetic Case: Built-in stand and screen protector for $39
Spigen Ultra Hybrid Pro: Clear case that’s MagSafe-compatible for $34
Home cameras for iPhone Duo StandBy mode
iPhone Duo will include a powerful upgrade to the current iPhone StandBy feature. When iPhone Duo is in “standing” mode, it can display a variety of StandBy views even when it’s not charging.
Those StandBy options include ‘Home Camera’ and ‘Home Modular’ views, both of which provide access to smart home accessories.
The Home Camera view should be especially useful for keeping track of security cameras throughout your home at a glance. Here are my recommended HomeKit-compatible cameras.
Aqara G100 2K security camera: Excellent budget-friendly camera that’s only $39
eufy 4K security camera: For 4K support, it’s not much pricier at just $59
What are some iPhone Duo accessories you plan to pick up? Let us know in the comments.

units.text: Shares in litigation funder Burford Capital jumped more than 9% today as a result of Apple’s $5.7 billion verdict over Taptic Engine patent infringement. Here are the details.
Apple verdict lifts litigation funder valuation
Last Friday, a US jury ruled that Apple’s Taptic Engine infringes on two patents held by California-based company Taction Technology.

Apple introduced the Taptic Engine in September 2014 with the first Apple Watch, and the technology has since expanded to other products, including the iPhone, where it provides haptic feedback for notifications, interactions, and other system events.

When Taction filed its patent infringement lawsuit in 2021, the company accused Apple of directly and indirectly infringing two of its patents through the Taptic Engine used in a range of iPhone and Apple Watch models.
Last Friday, following the verdict, Taction said the jury had “vindicated its patent rights,” while Apple said it strongly disagreed with the decision and would appeal.

Earlier today, as reported by The Financial Times, litigation funder Burford Capital disclosed that it has a financial entitlement in the case, and that it could be entitled to $1.4 billion if the $5.7 billion verdict is ultimately paid in full.
The disclosure sent Burford shares sharply higher in London, with the stock closing up 9.41% and giving the company a market capitalization of £659.9 million, or roughly $875 million.

Bloomberg Law notes that court records show that Taction received funding from Kenosha Investments LP and Gronostaj Investments LLC. The report also notes that Kenosha has been identified as an indirect subsidiary of Burford, which finances lawsuits in exchange for a share of any eventual recovery.

In a statement to investors on Monday, Burford said that if the $5.7 billion verdict were paid in full, its $1.4 billion entitlement would be split roughly equally between the company’s own balance sheet and its investment funds.

units.text: 随着苹果首款折叠屏手机iPhone Duo发布日期临近，其专属StandBy待机模式的更多细节被提前曝光。最新泄露信息显示，苹果实际上准备了多款尚未公开的新界面，使这一功能远比发布会上展示的内容更加丰富。
此前苹果已经确认，iPhone Duo将搭载专门优化的StandBy模式。与现有iPhone不同，新系统即使在没有连接充电器的情况下也能启用。得益于折叠结构，用户可以将手机半展开摆放，让设备自然形成支架形态，持续显示各种信息内容。
根据开发者通过iOS 27.1测试代码发现的信息，苹果至少还隐藏了五款尚未公布的新StandBy界面，分别被命名为Home Camera、Home Modular、Flow、Fade以及Snoopy。
其中最实用的新功能是Home Camera。该界面能够直接显示智能家居摄像头画面，既支持单一路实时监控，也能够同时显示最多九个摄像头组成的监控矩阵。对于已经使用HomeKit生态的用户而言，iPhone Duo在待机状态下几乎可以直接充当监控显示终端。
另一款名为Home Modular的界面则被认为与智能家居控制中心有关。虽然苹果尚未公布具体功能，但从命名和代码信息来看，它很可能用于集中管理家庭设备、智能场景以及各类家庭自动化控制项目。
与此同时，苹果还开发了两款更加神秘的新界面。
其中Flow似乎与动态艺术效果有关，相关代码中出现了“响应式艺术”等描述，意味着界面可能会根据时间、环境或者用户操作产生变化。至于Fade，目前尚未发现明确功能信息，具体用途仍然未知。
此外，苹果还准备了一款Snoopy主题界面。考虑到近年来苹果持续强化《花生漫画》相关合作，这套界面预计将采用动画风格，为待机模式增添更多娱乐和个性化元素。
